title: Restore unassisted erectile function after a finite treatment

concept.text: Durably restore erections in chronic vasculogenic or post-prostatectomy ED after treatment has ended. Regenerative approaches have clinical signals, but reliable, durable recovery without erection aids remains unestablished. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval for restoration of untreated function following a sham-controlled pivotal trial of at least 300 men: at least 50% achieve normal-range IIEF-EF scores and successful unassisted intercourse at 12 months, after at least three months without erection aids. Post-prostatectomy efficacy requires a separately powered analysis. Test set by: Proposed editorial completion test using validated sexual-function outcomes; FDA would decide an approval claim. EAU and SMSNA identify the need for better controlled evidence on restorative therapies. Sources given: [EAU erectile dysfunction guideline](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/sexual-and-reproductive-health/chapter/management-of-erectile-dysfunction) ; [SMSNA restorative-therapy position statement](https://academic.oup.com/smoa/article/9/3/100343/6956862).

page.title: Restoration of unassisted erectile function
page.definition: A finite treatment restores erections sufficient for intercourse in men with chronic vasculogenic erectile dysfunction, caused by impaired penile blood flow, or erectile dysfunction after radical prostatectomy, removal of the prostate and seminal vesicles. Erections continue after treatment ends without erection drugs, injections, vacuum devices or penile implants. Penile arterial reconstruction can already restore unassisted intercourse in selected young men with a local arterial blockage, otherwise healthy blood vessels and normal retention of blood during erection.

goal.need: After radical prostatectomy, 25–75% of men experience erectile dysfunction. Men with impaired penile blood flow or erectile dysfunction after surgery may rely on tablets, injections or a vacuum device for intercourse. Most men and their partners prefer spontaneous erections. Lasting recovery would let them have intercourse without arranging medication or a device. After prostatectomy, even men who regain erections have dry orgasms because the glands that make most of the seminal fluid have been removed.

completion.title: A regulator authorises a finite treatment for sustained unassisted erectile recovery.
completion.criterion: A regulator authorises a finite treatment with an indication explicitly covering sustained erections sufficient for intercourse after treatment ends, without erection drugs, injections, vacuum devices or penile implants. The authorised population and demonstrated treatment-free duration must be specified in the indication or supporting assessment. Achievement is recorded separately for vasculogenic and post-prostatectomy erectile dysfunction; an authorisation for one does not establish the other.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, following SMSNA's support for regulatory evaluation of restorative treatments; no common restoration-specific completion threshold was found.
completion.basis: Searches of EAU and SMSNA recommendations, FDA development requirements and trial registrations found no common cure test specifying a responder fraction, washout interval and duration after finite treatment. SMSNA supports regulatory approval based on safety and efficacy studies. The fallback requires authorisation for the restorative capability itself, with product-specific evidence defining its duration.

milestones.title: A candidate improves nerve-stimulated penile pressure relative to blood pressure at P < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: In a rat model of erectile dysfunction, cavernous nerve stimulation produces a greater increase in intracavernous pressure relative to mean arterial pressure in treated animals than in vehicle-treated controls (P < 0.05). In the cavernous nerve injury protocol, measure the response four weeks after injection and use the largest evoked pressure increase for each animal.
milestones.set_by: University of California, San Francisco, published controlled animal-study protocol of Albersen et al.; its four-week timing concerns cavernous-nerve injury. ESSM endorses ICP/MAP measurement, without defining a universal recovery cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: Results were considered statistically significant if p<0.05.

milestones.title: Men receive a finite restorative treatment in a phase I study with prospective safety follow-up.
milestones.criterion: Men receive a finite treatment under an approved phase I protocol with safety and tolerability as its primary endpoint. Investigators prospectively record adverse events through the protocol’s follow-up period. In the post-prostatectomy cell-therapy protocol, follow-up continued for six months after a single injection.
milestones.set_by: Odense University Hospital, registered phase I protocol NCT02240823, published for post-prostatectomy ED.
milestones.threshold_quote: Primary endpoint was the safety and tolerance of the cell therapy

milestones.title: More men than with placebo gain ≥2 or ≥5 erectile-function points, by baseline severity, at six months.
milestones.criterion: Six months after the final treatment, a greater proportion of treated men than placebo recipients must meet the response threshold in the per-protocol analysis (two-sided P < 0.05). Participants withhold all other erectile dysfunction treatments throughout the trial. On the six-item erectile-function domain of the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-EF), response requires a gain of ≥2 points from a baseline score of 17–25 or ≥5 points from a baseline score of 11–16.
milestones.set_by: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, registered protocol NCT04050020; written for mild-to-moderate nonsurgical ED and excluding previous major pelvic surgery.
milestones.threshold_quote: patients in each group attaining MCID in the IIEF-EF domain from baseline to 6 months after the final treatment.

milestones.title: More men than with placebo reach IIEF-EF ≥22 after six weeks without the study drug.
milestones.criterion: In a randomised placebo-controlled study, a significantly greater proportion of treated men must score ≥22 on the erectile-function domain of the International Index of Erectile Function after a six-week drug-free interval. REACTT defined this endpoint for men with normal preoperative erectile function who received nine months of treatment after bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, REACTT protocol NCT01026818; this recovery definition was published for early rehabilitation after bilateral nerve-sparing prostatectomy.

milestones.title: A multicentre trial meets SMSNA's 2-, 5- or 7-point median erectile-function efficacy thresholds.
milestones.criterion: A prospective, adequately powered, multicentre randomised sham- or placebo-controlled trial assesses safety and unassisted erectile function after finite treatment. The treatment group’s median post-treatment IIEF-EF score must exceed the control group’s median by ≥2 points for mild, ≥5 for moderate or ≥7 for severe erectile dysfunction. For mixed severity, apply the SMSNA severity-weighted threshold. Report how long participants remained off treatment and which erection aids were prohibited at each assessment.
milestones.set_by: SMSNA, 2026 position statement defining clinical efficacy, combined with its 2021 requirement for multicentre restorative-therapy safety and efficacy studies; these efficacy thresholds do not define cure.
milestones.threshold_quote: 2-, 5-, or 7-point median improvements between groups among mild, moderate, or severe ED cohorts

milestones.title: More men than with sham report penetration and completed intercourse on at least 2 of 4 attempts.
milestones.criterion: At three-month follow-up, compare the proportions of men answering yes at least twice to each of two Sexual Encounter Profile diary questions over four attempts in the preceding four weeks. Question 2 asks about vaginal penetration and question 3 asks whether the erection lasted long enough for successful intercourse. Participants report no erection-drug use during follow-up. The treated proportion must exceed the sham proportion at P < 0.05.
milestones.set_by: Ortac and colleagues, Istanbul University, in the trial registered with the Turkish Ministry of Health as 71146310 (2014-MDD-CE-55) for mild vasculogenic erectile dysfunction.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least two “yes” answers to each SEP2 and SEP3 question

not_found: No common regulator or society completion test specified a responder fraction, treatment-free interval and durability period for restoration after finite ED treatment.
ClinicalTrials.gov records NCT01026818 and NCT02240823 rendered without study details; their endpoints were available in the peer-reviewed reports.
The full AUANews account of the 2026 SMSNA restorative-therapy update could not be opened.

results.finding: In 63 rats with cavernous nerve crush, both immediate and delayed stromal vascular fraction injections increased stimulated penile pressure relative to arterial pressure versus saline (P < 0.05).
results.detail: The delayed group received its injection four weeks after nerve crush. Both groups had their pressure response measured 12 weeks after crush.
results.quote: This was reflected by significantly increased ICP/MAP responses to cavernous nerve electrostimulation compared to the vehicle group.

results.finding: Among 40 phase I participants treated with autologous bone marrow concentrate, 0 had a serious adverse event through six months.
results.detail: The 40 participants were split evenly between two dose groups. The parallel registry enrolled another 100 men.

results.finding: In the parallel registry of 100 men with PDE5 inhibitor-refractory erectile dysfunction, mean IIEF-5 improved by 9 points at six months.
results.detail: The registry improvement was pooled across a heterogeneous cohort. The paper describes participants as receiving optimized medical therapy and does not document that they withheld all other erectile dysfunction treatments.
results.quote: Mean improvements in IIEF-5 score were 2 in the Caverstem 1.0 low dose group, 3 in the high dose Caverstem 1.0 group and 9 in the Caverstem 2.0 group. Furthermore, improvements peaked by 3 months and maintained at 6 months follow-up.

results.finding: Among 21 men treated with autologous adipose-derived regenerative cells for post-prostatectomy erectile dysfunction, zero serious adverse events occurred.
results.detail: The abstract identifies safety as the primary endpoint. It gives no protocol approval information and does not explicitly identify tolerability as part of that endpoint.
results.quote: No serious adverse events occurred, but 8 reversible minor events related to the liposuction were noted.
